claim: For \(0\le a<b<\infty\), \(\lambda>0\), and every nonzero finite positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \([a,b]\), define \(S_{\lambda,\mu}(z)=\int_{[a,b]}(z+t)^{-\lambda}\,d\mu(t)\) on \(\Omega_a=\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,-a]\), using the principal branch. Set \(\Theta(z)=|\arg(z+a)-\arg(z+b)|\) for \(z\in\Omega_a\). A point \(z\) is a zero of \(S_{\lambda,\mu}\) for some such \(\mu\) if and only if \(\Theta(z)\ge\pi/\lambda\); whenever this holds, a positive measure with at most two atoms realizes the zero. Thus the universal zero locus is empty for \(0<\lambda\le1\), and for \(\lambda=2\) it is the nonreal part of the disk with diameter \([-b,-a]\).

correctness.rationale: The proof handles the real domain separately, uses strict half-plane separation when \(\lambda\Theta(z)<\pi\), and constructs a positive two-atom measure with opposite kernel phases when \(\lambda\Theta(z)\ge\pi\). The argument is exact for every \(\lambda>0\) and every allowed compact interval.

evidence: The theorem covers every real \(\lambda>0\) and every nonzero finite positive measure on a fixed compact interval.
The two-atom construction attains every point in the region, including the boundary \(\Theta(z)=\pi/\lambda\).

value.rationale: The attainable zero region is a natural exact invariant for cancellation in positive mixtures of fractional resolvent kernels. The theorem gives the sharp order threshold \(\lambda=1\), the complete visual-angle region for every order, and a two-atom realizing measure at each admissible point, which is useful for zero localization and stability analysis.
